entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Jacques II de Goyon seigneur de Matignon (1525-1598) was a governor and Marshal of France. Coming from a prominent Norman family, he assumed the role of Lieutenant-General of lower Normandy.

Matignon came into conflict with the Protestant governor of Normandy, Bouillon, during the first civil war. He also clashed with the French crown, which sought to reassert control over the region.

Despite these challenges, Matignon maintained a strong presence in Normandy, and his legacy as a military leader endured for centuries.

Matignon's life was marked by both triumph and tragedy, including his role in the Battle of Dreux, where he fought alongside King Henry III against the Huguenots.

In 1574, Matignon was appointed governor of Normandy, a position he held until his death on July 27, 1598.
